original_question: For a circle of radius n, determine the maximum number of unit circles, each tangent to at most two others, that can be packed inside it. More generally, solve the corresponding extremal packing problems for circles of radius phi(n), for circles in a triangle, and for analogous packings of spheres, cones, cylinders, regular pyramids, and more general plane or spatial figures inside a prescribed container.
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, "Maximum number of circles": the open problem asking for the maximum number of circles of radius 1, "at most twice tangential," contained in a circle of radius n, together with the immediately following generalization to circles of radius Φ(n) and the analogous variants for a given triangle and for higher-dimensional figures.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's core target very closely: the container is a circle of radius n; the packed objects are unit circles; the objective is extremal (maximize the number packed); the tangency restriction is the paper's informal "at most twice tangential" condition; and you also correctly include the same-paragraph extensions to circles of radius Φ(n), to a given triangle, and to analogous problems for spheres, cones, cylinders, regular pyramids, and more general planar or spatial figures.
missing_details: The paper states the constraint informally as "at most twice tangential"; to make the question stand-alone, this should be spelled out as a condition on tangencies among the packed circles, namely that each packed circle is tangent to at most two other packed circles.
The paper does not explicitly say "packing"; non-overlap (equivalently, pairwise interior-disjointness of the packed circles) is implicit and should be made explicit in a refined formulation.
The quantifier on n is implicit: the statement is for a prescribed radius n, but the paper does not specify whether n is assumed to be an integer or an arbitrary positive real number.

For the generalized version, the paper only says that Φ is a function of n; it does not impose positivity, monotonicity, asymptotics, or any other regularity assumptions, so these should not be added.
The triangle variant is for circles of radius 1 in a given triangle, and the paper explicitly links this to Malfatti's problem; that contextual cue is absent from the draft.

For the higher-dimensional analogues, the paper gives only an informal extension ('similar questions' for spheres, cones, cylinders, regular pyramids, etc.; more generally for plane figures in a given planar figure, and in space too), so the refined question should preserve that limited scope rather than impose extra formal structure not stated in the paper.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity condition, degree restriction, or nilpotency hypothesis is part of the paper's statement; this is a purely geometric extremal-packing problem.
refined_question: Given a prescribed circle of radius n, determine the maximum number of pairwise non-overlapping circles of radius 1 that can be contained in it under the condition that each packed circle is tangent to at most two other packed circles. In the same sense, determine the corresponding extremal problem for circles of radius Φ(n), where Φ is a given function of n, contained in a circle of radius n; for circles of radius 1 contained in a given triangle (in the spirit of Malfatti's problem); and analogously for spheres, cones, cylinders, regular pyramids, and, more generally, for prescribed plane figures inside a prescribed planar figure, and in space as well.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's actual wording in §2.1. The paper is not developing a broader theory here; it simply records an open extremal-packing question and then appends a Bencze generalization and a list of analogous variants in the same paragraph. The only paper-faithful sharpening needed is to make explicit the implied non-overlap condition and to unpack the informal phrase "at most twice tangential" as a tangency-degree-at-most-two condition. I did not add extra hypotheses on n or on Φ, because the paper itself does not supply them, and I kept the triangle and spatial variants only because they are explicitly included in the same §2.1 statement.

citations.label: Bencze generalization to Φ(n); triangle (Malfatti) and spatial variants
